column4: Visit note | 2025-12-07 04:00 PM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Arif Siddique, 31, male. Mr. Siddique returns for a clinical review of his ongoing condition, reporting that he still experiences sudden attacks of a racing heart and an intense fear of dying. He works as a cricket coach, and he explains that these alarming episodes initially began following a stressful traffic accident in Keraniganj. He states that he has suffered about 8 panic attacks in the last month. He denies any chest pressure, suicidal ideation, or hallucinations, and he confirms he has no other major medical illnesses. On clinical examination, his vital signs are as follows: BP 133/71 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 87 kg. His mood is anxious, but his thought process is coherent and he is fully oriented. Assessment: Panic disorder. Plan: chronic follow-up: continue current medicines, no new prescription issued. No new medicine was prescribed during this appointment. He was advised to practise slow breathing during attacks, reduce caffeine intake, and start professional counselling sessions. Follow-up is scheduled in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-12-18 02:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Rokeya Sultana, 78, female. Mrs. Sultana visits the clinic complaining of an uncomfortable tingling sensation like pins and needles accompanied by a persistent burning in both feet. She is a retired civil servant, and she mentions that these symptoms started after years of high blood sugar that was first detected at a health camp in Tongi. She has a known history of Bronchial asthma, but she denies any recent chest wheezing or acute breathing difficulty. On examination, neurological testing reveals reduced sensation at 4 of 10 monofilament test sites. Her other vitals are: BP 123/78 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 81 kg. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: HbA1c, vitamin B12, and a nerve conduction study. No new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to check her feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep her blood sugar under tight control. Follow-up is scheduled after the test results are ready.
